title: Temu in Pakistan: How It Works, Shipping & Alternatives
summary: How Temu works in Pakistan, what its shipping route and customs really involve, and the alternatives for shoppers and resellers who need COD.
body_markdown:
Temu is a cross-border shopping app. Chinese sellers list their stock on it, Temu sets the price and runs the logistics, and every order you place ships to you from China as an individual parcel. That last part is the whole story in Pakistan. There is no local warehouse here, no rupee checkout and no cash on delivery, so a Pakistani order becomes an international parcel that you pay for by card in a foreign currency and then wait on.


This guide takes the model apart, walks the shipping route leg by leg — including the customs bill nobody quotes you — then sorts the alternatives by the job you are hiring one for: shopping, reselling, or buying at wholesale tiers. If you only want the short answer on whether orders get through,[is Temu available in Pakistan](https://www.markaz.app/blog-post/is-temu-available-in-pakistan) covers that on its own.


## How Temu actually works


Most people meet Temu through an ad showing a price that looks impossible. The price is usually real. Understanding why it is real tells you exactly where the model helps you and where it stops.


### The sellers are Chinese factories and traders, not local shops


Temu is operated by PDD Holdings, the same group behind Pinduoduo in China. Sellers ship stock into Temu's system and Temu handles the listing, the pricing and the delivery to your door. There is no importer, no distributor and no retailer between the factory and you. Every layer of margin that a product normally collects on its way to a shop shelf has been removed from the number you see.


### Why the prices look the way they do


Four things push the sticker down at once:


- **You are buying at close to the source tier.** The factory or the trader lists directly. Nobody in between marks it up.
- **The goods are chosen for freight economics.** Look at what the app pushes hardest — phone accessories, jewellery, small home items, kitchen gadgets. Light, flat, unbreakable. Those are the categories where sending one parcel across the world barely moves the unit cost.
- **Sellers compete on price inside the app.** The listing that wins visibility is usually the one that undercuts, which drives the whole category down.
- **Marketing spend buys the first order, not the margin.** An aggressive launch price is a customer-acquisition cost, and it is not the price the model has to sustain forever.


None of that is a trick. It is a genuine retail model built for markets where Temu has set up local payment, local delivery and local returns. Pakistan is not one of those markets yet.


### What Temu does not do in Pakistan


Three things are missing, and each one costs you something specific:


- **No rupee checkout and no cash on delivery.** You pay in advance, by card, in a foreign currency.
- **No local stock.** Nothing is sitting in a Pakistani warehouse, so nothing arrives in days.
- **No local support or returns address.** If a parcel goes missing or an item is wrong, there is no office in Lahore or Karachi to chase.


The prices survive the trip to Pakistan. The convenience that makes those prices worth having does not.


## Shipping to Pakistan: what the route actually involves


"Shipping" is a single line on a checkout page and four separate operations in reality. Knowing the legs tells you where an order stalls and who you can ask about it.


### The four legs of a cross-border parcel


1. **Domestic China leg.** The seller ships your item to a consolidation warehouse inside China. This is fast and almost never the problem.
2. **Consolidation and line-haul.** Your parcel waits to be packed with others going the same way, then moves by air or sea. Waiting for the shipment to fill is where most of the "why has nothing happened for days" time goes.
3. **Destination customs.** The shipment arrives in Pakistan and has to clear. Nothing you do speeds this up.
4. **Last-mile delivery.** A local courier takes it from the clearing point to your door.


Tracking usually looks healthy on legs one and four and goes quiet in the middle. That silence is normal for cross-border shipping and it is also why a fixed promise date is hard for anyone to give you. For how the same route behaves when someone else runs it end to end, see[China to Pakistan delivery times](https://www.markaz.app/blog-post/china-to-pakistan-delivery-time) .


### Customs, duty and the bill nobody quotes you


Goods entering Pakistan can attract customs duty, sales tax and other levies. What you pay depends on what the item is, how it is classified and what value is declared on the paperwork. Courier shipments are often cleared on your behalf with the charges billed to you on delivery, which is how a "cheap" order turns into an argument at the door.


Two practical rules. First, check the current tariff treatment for your product category before you order rather than assuming the checkout total is the final number — rates change and they are not the same across categories. Second, never ask a seller to under-declare a value to reduce the charge. It puts the shipment at risk and it puts you at risk.


### Payment: the card wall


A cross-border app needs a card enabled for international transactions. Plenty of Pakistani shoppers do not have one, and plenty who do would still rather not pay in advance for something coming from another country. This is not a small preference. Cash on delivery is the default way Pakistan buys online, and any platform that cannot offer it is asking for trust before it has earned any.


### Returns are the part that actually hurts


A wrong size is a small annoyance domestically and an expensive one across a border. Sending an item back to China costs more than most low-priced items are worth, so in practice a bad order is written off rather than returned. Price that risk in before you order. If safety and recourse are your main concern,[ordering from China safely in Pakistan](https://www.markaz.app/blog-post/is-it-safe-to-order-from-china-pakistan) goes through the checks worth making.


## What this means if you want to resell Temu products


Sourcing stock to resell is a different job from shopping, and the same model that makes Temu attractive to a shopper works against a reseller.


- **You are buying at retail.** Temu is pointed at end consumers. A reseller needs to buy below retail, and the wholesale tiers sit further up the chain on domestic Chinese platforms.
- **Lead time fights cash on delivery.** A Pakistani customer who orders on COD expects the parcel soon, not after an international transit. Pre-selling a long wait is possible but it raises refusals badly.
- **You pay before you know it sells.** Card payment up front means your capital is stuck in stock you have not tested.
- **No invoice, no warranty, no replacement path.** When your customer has a complaint, you absorb it.


That does not make cross-border sourcing wrong. It makes single-parcel retail sourcing wrong. If you are pricing a reselling business properly,[how landed cost really works for Pakistani sellers](https://www.markaz.app/blog-post/cheaper-than-aliexpress-smarter-sourcing-in-pakistan) breaks down the six components that decide whether a cheap sticker is actually cheap.

The mechanics are simple. On the China side, Markaz buys, imports, clears and delivers, and you see one price in rupees with cash on delivery — roughly ten to seventeen days to the door, no agent to appoint, no clearance to arrange.[The China deals page](https://www.markaz.app/china/deals) is the fastest way to see what is moving right now. That is the honest trade. A cross-border app gives you the widest possible catalogue and asks you to carry the payment risk, the wait and the customs uncertainty yourself. The Markaz model narrows the catalogue to what can actually be delivered here and carries those three things for you.


## Before you order from any cross-border app: a checklist


1. Add the shipping charge to the item price before you decide anything is cheap.
2. Check how duty and sales tax are treated for that product category, and assume the charge will be billed on delivery.
3. Confirm your card is enabled for international transactions, and check what the currency conversion adds.
4. Read the return policy for your country, not the one in the marketing copy.
5. Ask yourself what happens if it never arrives. If the answer is "nothing I can do", cap the order value accordingly.
6. If you are reselling, price the wait and the refusal risk into your margin — not just the unit cost.


## Frequently asked questions


### Does Temu deliver to Pakistan?


Temu does not operate a localized Pakistani service the way it does in markets where it has built out local payment, warehousing and returns. Orders sometimes get through, but as an international parcel — paid by card in a foreign currency, subject to customs, with no local support behind it.


### Can I pay cash on delivery on Temu?


No. Cross-border checkout is card-based and paid in advance. If cash on delivery is what you need, you need a platform that holds stock or handles the import locally.


### Will I be charged customs on a Temu order?


You can be. Duty and taxes depend on the product category, its classification and the declared value, and courier shipments are frequently cleared with the charges billed to you on arrival. Treat the checkout total as a floor, not a final price.


### Is Temu cheaper than buying locally in Pakistan?


On the sticker, often. Landed at your door with shipping, conversion charges and any duty added, the gap narrows and sometimes closes — especially on anything heavy or bulky. Compare the total you actually pay, not the listing price.


### Can I resell Temu products in Pakistan?


You can, but the economics are against you. You are buying at retail tier, paying before you have sold anything, and asking a cash-on-delivery customer to wait through an international transit. Sourcing from stock that is already in Pakistan, or from a platform that handles the import for you, fits how Pakistan buys much better.


### What is the closest thing to Temu that works properly in Pakistan?


A platform that gives you China-sourced products priced in rupees, with cash on delivery and door-to-door delivery handled end to end. That is what Markaz China does, and it is the reason the comparison comes up so often.
